stories.blurb: The Sussex County Fairgrounds website says the Farm and Horse Show was incorporated as a nonprofit on April 26, 1940. <short pause> It says the fair was not held from 1942 to 1945 because of World War II. <short pause> It says Hurricane Connie hit the old grounds during the fair in 1955. <short pause> It says the directors bought 126 acres in Augusta in 1963 for $55,000 and held opening ceremonies for the new fairgrounds in August of 1976. <short pause> Wikipedia says it is now a 10-day fair every August, attracting about 220,000 people a year.
stories.flag: Origin year differs by source (horse shows from 1919 to 1924 versus the 1940 fair), so only the 1940 incorporation is given. The old grounds were in Branchville.
music: Overcast by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Hampton Splits From Newton
stories.blurb: The New Jersey Herald says lawmakers approved the act creating this township on March 10th, 1864. <short pause> It was one of three new municipalities cut from Newton Township. <short pause> The Herald says what prompted the split remains uncertain. <short pause> It says Colonel Robert Hamilton was named as the prime mover. <short pause> A history of Sussex County says the township was named for a man who donated land to the Episcopal Church in Newton. <short pause> Its only villages are Washingtonville and Balesville.
music: Night Cave by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Governor Who Settled in Hamburg
stories.blurb: The borough of Hamburg calls Governor Daniel Haines its most famous citizen. <short pause> It says he settled in Hamburg at age 23 as a lawyer. <short pause> The National Governors Association says his first term as governor began on October 27, 1843. <short pause> The borough says he also served 14 years as a justice of the state Supreme Court. <short pause> The National Governors Association says he died on January 26, 1877. <short pause> A published obituary says he died at his home in Hamburg.
music: Almost in F by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Gingerbread Castle
stories.blurb: The Gingerbread Castle stands beside the old Wheatsworth Mill in Hamburg. <short pause> Preservation New Jersey says mill owner F.H. Bennett built it between 1928 and 1930. <short pause> It says the Viennese architect Joseph Urban designed it. <short pause> The borough says it cost $250,000. <short pause> Time magazine reported in July of 1930 that hundreds of children came through the gates. <short pause> Time described a white roof like sugar icing and cork cookies set in the walls.
music: Shaving Mirror by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Wallings, Sharpsboro and Hamburg
stories.blurb: The borough of Hamburg says its earliest known settler, Joseph Walling Sr., came around 1740 and built an inn. <short pause> It says that for a short time, the town was called Wallings in his honor. <short pause> A Sussex County historical marker says Joseph Sharp built a forge and furnace on the Wallkill River in 1768. <short pause> The borough dates the Sharp Iron Works to around 1770. <short pause> The marker says the village around the iron works later became Hamburg.
stories.flag: SINGLE for the Wallings name: borough page only. The forge date is attributed to both sources because they differ.
music: Fluidscape by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Napoleon's Brother at Point Breeze
stories.blurb: Joseph Bonaparte, the older brother of Napoleon, lived in Bordentown during his years in America. <short pause> The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia dates his stay from 1815 to 1839. <short pause> He built an estate called Point Breeze. <short pause> The encyclopedia says the first of his two grand houses burned in 1820. <short pause> It says visitors included the Marquis de Lafayette. <short pause> The Philadelphia Inquirer reported in 2021 that the old gardener's house is the only building still standing and that 55 acres now belong to the public.
music: Opium by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Paine, Rails and a Canal
stories.blurb: Bordentown is named for Joseph Borden, who bought most of the local land in 1717. <short pause> The Delaware River Heritage Trail says Thomas Paine lived there on and off from 1777 to 1803. <short pause> It says that in 1831 and 32, Bordentown became the southern end of the first section of the Camden and Amboy Railroad. <short pause> The trail calls it the third railroad built in the United States. <short pause> It says the 44-mile Delaware and Raritan Canal opened in 1834.
stories.flag: SINGLE: Delaware River Heritage Trail page for the railroad and canal facts.
music: Special Spotlight by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Iron Works That Fitted Paris
stories.blurb: Florence Township says a company bought 600 acres in 1849. <short pause> It says the Florence Iron Works was started in 1857. <short pause> The township says Richard Wood bought the plant in 1867. <short pause> It says his company created most of the present water and sewer systems. <short pause> The township says the company exported pipe, hydrants, and valves to Europe. <short pause> It says much of Paris was fitted with equipment forged there.
stories.flag: SINGLE: township history page only. The Paris claim is the township's.
music: Crunk Knight by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Company Town Built by Roebling
stories.blurb: Roebling is a company town, named for John Roebling. <short pause> The New Jersey Historic Trust says the Roebling mill made wire rope and cable for the George Washington Bridge and the Golden Gate Bridge. <short pause> It says the mill covered 160 acres, with a planned community beside it for its workers. <short pause> The state says construction began in 1905, and the Roebling Historical Society says ground was broken in 1904. <short pause> The plant closed in 1974. <short pause> The state says a 20-year, $70 million federal cleanup followed, and the main gatehouse became the Roebling Museum.
music: Brain Dance by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Town Founded on a Promise of Liberty
stories.blurb: Burlington City history says Belgian Walloons built the first recorded European settlement in New Jersey around 1624, a trading post on an island. <short pause> It says the proprietors authorized the town on March 3rd, 1677. <short pause> The city says their founding document set out civil and religious liberty. <short pause> It says the document also called for an elected assembly and freedom of speech. <short pause> An 1877 oration says settlers from the ship Kent laid out the town that year.
music: Comfortable Mystery by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Don't Give Up the Ship
stories.blurb: The Crossroads of the American Revolution site says Captain James Lawrence was born in a house on High Street in Burlington on October 1st, 1781. <short pause> It says he was the youngest of 11 children. <short pause> It says he was educated in law but joined the young Navy in September of 1798 as a midshipman. <short pause> It says he famously shouted, "Tell the men to fire faster and not to give up the ship. Fight her till she sinks." <short pause> It says the Navy has named five ships after him.
stories.flag: Single source: Crossroads of the American Revolution site.
music: Crisis by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Prison Robert Mills Designed
stories.blurb: The county seat moved from Burlington City to Mount Holly in 1795. <short pause> The Burlington County Prison Museum says the freeholders voted in 1806 to build a county jail there. <short pause> It says the architect Robert Mills designed it. <short pause> The museum says Mills designed it around the Quaker idea that inmates could be reformed through religious instruction, education, and job training. <short pause> The National Historic Landmark nomination says the prison has changed little since it was built in 1810 and 1811.
music: Mystic Force by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Batsto, the Iron Village of the Pine Barrens
stories.blurb: Batsto Village grew around an iron furnace founded in 1766. <short pause> The village's own history says it ran on bog ore from the streams, charcoal from the forest, and water power. <short pause> It says the works made pots and kettles and supplies for the Continental Army. <short pause> The state says those supplies included cannon and mortars. <short pause> Joseph Wharton bought Batsto in 1876. <short pause> The village history says the last house was emptied in 1989.
music: Sancho Panza gets a Latte by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Where the Blueberry Was First Grown for Sale
stories.blurb: Whitesbog, in Pemberton Township, was a large cranberry farm. <short pause> The New Jersey Pinelands Commission says Elizabeth White, the owner's daughter, invited the botanist Frederick Coville to experiment there. <short pause> The commission says she asked local people to find wild bushes with large berries and paid cash rewards. <short pause> The U.S. Department of Agriculture says Coville had learned that blueberries need acidic soil. <short pause> Both agencies say the first cultivated crop was harvested in 1916. <short pause> The commission says White was also the first to package the fruit in clear cellophane.
music: Lobby Time by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Mexican Lindbergh and the Pine Barrens Monument
stories.blurb: In 1928, the Mexican aviator Captain Emilio Carranza flew to New York on a goodwill flight. <short pause> Journey Through Jersey says it was a reply to Charles Lindbergh's flight the year before. <short pause> On the flight home that July, his plane was caught in a thunderstorm over the Pine Barrens, and he died in the crash. <short pause> A monument marks the spot in Tabernacle. <short pause> A state history says it was paid for by gifts from Mexican school children. <short pause> A memorial ceremony is held there each July.
music: Agnus Dei X by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: A Name That Means Sweet Water
stories.blurb: The township of Cinnaminson says its name comes from the Lenape. <short pause> It says the Lenape called their hunting grounds Cinnaminson, which meant sweet water. <short pause> A list of Burlington County place names also gives the meaning as sweet water. <short pause> The township says the state created it on March 15th, 1860, by dividing Chester Township.
music: Truth in the Stones by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Village That Began With a Road
stories.blurb: Moorestown says property owners were here as early as 1680. <short pause> The township says the village was founded in 1682 when the first owners built homes and lived here. <short pause> Its preservation plan says the village began with the surveying and clearing of Salem Road between Burlington and Salem. <short pause> The township says the first Friends meeting house, built of logs, went up on King's Highway in 1700. <short pause> The National Register nomination says the early settlers were Quakers.
music: Pamgaea by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: From Upper Evesham to Medford
stories.blurb: Medford was first a village in Evesham Township, known as Upper Evesham. <short pause> New Jersey Slavery Records says the name Medford became attached to the village in the early 1800s. <short pause> The township says the legislature set it apart from Evesham on February 4, 1847. <short pause> It says the first township meeting was held on March 9 at the Crossroads. <short pause> Wikipedia lists the township's incorporation as March 1. <short pause> The Slavery Records site says Medford Lakes was taken from it in 1939.
music: Rollin at 5 by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: YMCA of the Pines
stories.blurb: The YMCA of the Pines, formerly a YMCA camp, was established in 1906. <short pause> The camp's own history says it was set up by the YMCAs of Burlington, Camden, Gloucester, and Monmouth counties. <short pause> It says the land held an abandoned mill and a cranberry bog in a forest of pine, oak, cedar, and laurel. <short pause> A South Jersey site says the camp found its permanent home in Medford in 1926 after several earlier locations. <short pause> The camp says that before that, it was held at sites on the Delaware River and in New Egypt. <short pause> It says a camp for girls opened in 1936.
music: Upbeat Forever by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Town Planned Before It Was Built
stories.blurb: Riverton was founded in 1851 by a group of 10 Philadelphians as a place for summer homes. <short pause> The borough says architect Samuel Sloan designed the village on 120 acres. <short pause> The plan included a seawall, a pier, and a railroad station, and made no provision for industry. <short pause> The borough says architectural historian Henry Russell Hitchcock called it the first totally planned residential subdivision in America.
music: Space 1990 by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Steamboat Landing and the Yacht Club
stories.blurb: The New Jersey Historic Trust says 10 Philadelphians established the borough in 1851 as a summer resort. <short pause> It says their company had a steamboat landing built that same year as the primary way to reach town. <short pause> It says residents formed a yacht club in 1865. <short pause> It says the club received permission in 1880 to build its clubhouse on the landing. <short pause> It says steamboat service ceased in 1917, and in 1918 the yacht club purchased the entire landing.
stories.flag: Single source: Landing, Riverton Yacht Club and steamboat dates are from the NJ Historic Trust page only.
music: Meditation Impromptu 03 by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Town That Dropped the Name Texas
stories.blurb: Palmyra was originally known as Texas. <short pause> The borough says landowner Isaiah Toy, a railroad stockholder, wanted a post office and thought the name Texas undignified. <short pause> It says he persuaded the Camden and Amboy Railroad to change the station name to Palmyra in 1849. <short pause> The borough says the name came from his love of ancient history, after an ancient city in Syria. <short pause> The post office opened in 1851.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the Isaiah Toy naming story: the borough website. Wikipedia confirms only the naming for Palmyra, Syria.
music: Errigal by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Court Case That Changed Housing Law
stories.blurb: In Mount Laurel in 1970, the mayor spoke to residents at Jacob's Chapel AME Church about low-income housing. <short pause> The New Jersey State Historical Briefing quotes him, "If you people can't afford to live in our town, then you'll just have to leave." <short pause> The briefing says that exchange helped start a lawsuit, Southern Burlington County NAACP versus Mount Laurel Township. <short pause> The New Jersey Supreme Court decided it on March 24, 1975. <short pause> The state lists a second ruling in 1983 as Mount Laurel II.
music: Isolated by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Delran Before 1880
stories.blurb: Delran Township's own history says the present name was given in 1880. <short pause> Before that, it says the area was part of Cinnaminson Township from 1860. <short pause> From 1692 to 1860, it was part of Chester Township.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the 1880 name date: the township history page. The 1860 Cinnaminson dates are confirmed by NJ Slavery Records.
music: Dub Feral by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Town That Was Renamed Levittown
stories.blurb: Willingboro began as the constabulary of Wellingborough in 1688. <short pause> The township says developer William Levitt's agents began buying land there in 1954. <short pause> By 1956, it says Levitt owned 90% of the township. <short pause> The Philadelphia Encyclopedia says he built 11,000 homes and sold the first in June of 1958. <short pause> It says residents voted to rename the town Levittown in 1959 and changed it back to Willingboro in 1963.
music: George Street Shuffle by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Ban on For Sale Signs
stories.blurb: In 1973, Willingboro banned "for sale" signs on lawns, according to the New Jersey Herald. <short pause> The Supreme Court's summary says the township acted to stem what it perceived as the flight of white homeowners from an integrated community. <short pause> On May 2, 1977, in Linmark Associates v. Willingboro, the U.S. Supreme Court held that the ordinance violated the First Amendment.
music: Midnight Tale by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Governor's Deer Park
stories.blurb: The township history says Sir William Franklin built a summer mansion and also a park for keeping deer in the old township. <short pause> It says he was the son of Benjamin Franklin and the last royal British governor of New Jersey. <short pause> A historical marker says he owned the property from 1770 to 1785. <short pause> A Revolutionary War sites guide says he served as royal governor from 1763 to 1776.
music: Clear Waters by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Town of Parks
stories.blurb: The Burlington County Times says the township was built in 1958 as a suburban community of parks under the developer William Levitt. <short pause> It says each park had its own school, playground, and pool. <short pause> It says the town gained 12 parks. <short pause> It says one park, school, and neighborhood opened first in 1958, with a second park following in 1959.
stories.flag: Single source: Burlington County Times, Oct. 9, 2018 (Willingboro; Somerset Park first, Buckingham Park second).
music: ZigZag by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Brimstone Neck, Quakertown, Vincentown
stories.blurb: Vincentown is a village in Southampton Township. <short pause> The township says it was once called Brimstone Neck and later Quakertown because of a large settlement of Quakers. <short pause> It says the present name dates to 1743 when Vincent Leeds bought most of the land where the village stands. <short pause> The town became known as Vincent's Town. <short pause> The township says its post office received its charter on April 22nd, 1824.
music: Spirit of the Girl by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Two Ideas About the Name
stories.blurb: Evesham Township says Welsh and English Quakers crossed the Delaware in the 1600s, looking for farmland and religious freedom. <short pause> It says Evesham was set up as a constabulary in 1688 and officially became a township in 1692. <short pause> The township says the name was first spelled Eversham. <short pause> It says many believe it was named for Evesham, England, a market town. <short pause> Wikipedia adds that it may instead have been named for a settler, Thomas Eves.
music: The Sky of our Ancestors by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Town Named for Its Lumber
stories.blurb: Lumberton was once known as Lumber Town. <short pause> The township historical society says the name came from the pine trees nearby and the boats and rafts that carried lumber and cordwood from Rancocas Creek to Philadelphia. <short pause> It says there were two or three lumber yards and sawmills at one time. <short pause> The society says that in 1683, an English physician, Robert Dimsdale, bought land from William Penn and built a small community around a sawmill.
stories.flag: SINGLE source: the township historical society page.
music: Bicycle by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: When Lumberton Split in Two
stories.blurb: The school district says that in the 1800s the township included what is now a neighboring township. <short pause> It says there were five schools in all with small one and two room buildings. <short pause> It says that in 1917 residents wanted one multi-room building for better educational opportunities. <short pause> It says the people of the neighboring community chose to keep their own school and the municipality divided in two. <short pause> Wikipedia says the neighboring township was formed on March 12th, 1924.
music: Nano Hoedown by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Civil War Hospital on the River
stories.blurb: In 1864, the federal government opened a military hospital in Beverly to relieve crowded Philadelphia hospitals. <short pause> The Department of Veterans Affairs says patients arrived from Philadelphia on the steamer John A. Warner. <short pause> It says that according to local lore, townspeople met the boat, church bells tolled, and women served food and coffee. <short pause> The hospital held up to 2,500 patients. It closed in 1865.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the hospital story: the Department of Veterans Affairs interpretive sign.
music: River Fire by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The National Cemetery Beside the River
stories.blurb: Beverly National Cemetery is in Edgewater Park. <short pause> The Department of Veterans Affairs says a private citizen gave the land to the federal government in August of 1864. <short pause> The first burial was on August 29th. <short pause> By the end of the Civil War, 147 soldiers were buried there, seven of them unknown. <short pause> On June 25th, 1875, a marble monument nearly 60 feet tall topped with a standing soldier was dedicated.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the 1864 and 1875 details: the Department of Veterans Affairs interpretive sign. Wikipedia confirms the location only and gives a different establishment year (1863), so none is stated.
music: Nightdreams by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Timbuctoo and the Underground Railroad
stories.blurb: Westampton Township has a historic village settled in 1826. <short pause> The township says settlement began when four African American men bought land from a Quaker businessman. <short pause> The New Jersey State Library says deeds in the county clerk's office confirm the first purchases in September of that year. <short pause> Both say the village's name first appeared on a deed in 1830. <short pause> The state library says the community had more than 125 people in the middle of the century and was a stop on the Underground Railroad.
music: Concentration by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Three J's of Springfield
stories.blurb: Springfield Township has three hamlets, known locally as the Three Js: Jacksonville, Jobstown, and Juliustown. <short pause> The township says it was founded by royal charter on November 6, 1688. <short pause> The historical society says the townships were set up that day as constabularies and that Springfield received its charter on January 13, 1713. <short pause> A place names book from 1955 says Jobstown was named for a tavern keeper, Job Lippincott.
music: Hypnothis by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Soldiers at the Quaker Meeting House
stories.blurb: The Quaker Meeting House in Crosswicks hosted two colonial councils about the Lenape in 1756 and 1758. <short pause> The site Crossroads of the American Revolution says the Lenape asked that the meetings be held in Crosswicks where they had trust with the local Quakers. <short pause> It says about 2,100 American troops stayed in and around the meeting house on December 29th, 1776. <short pause> It says General John Cadwalader later got a letter from George Washington ordering him to march to Trenton. <short pause> The site says that through the war the building housed troops from both sides on the understanding that the Quakers kept Sunday worship free.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the December 1776 troop detail: Crossroads of the American Revolution. The 1756 and 1758 councils are in both sources.
music: Mountain Emperor by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Cannonball in the Meeting House Wall
stories.blurb: The Liberty Trail says the Friends Meeting House in the village was completed in 1773. <short pause> It says that on June 23rd, 1778, British forces clashed with New Jersey militia near the village. <short pause> It says the militia retreated across the creek and dismantled the bridge. <short pause> The site says a cannonball is still embedded in the north wall between the second-story windows. <short pause> It says it is unknown whether the British or the Continentals fired it.
stories.flag: Single source: Cannonball detail and June 23, 1778 date are from the Liberty Trail page only (Crosswicks Friends Meeting House).
music: Adventure Meme by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Soda That Helped the Medicine Go Down
stories.blurb: The Riverside Historical Society says that in 1913, a pharmacist named Benjamin Faunce invented Tak-A-Boost. <short pause> It says he served it at his Bridgeboro Street pharmacy to help the medicine go down easier. <short pause> The society says the citrus syrup, now called Boost, is still a popular thirst quencher. <short pause> The Delaware River Heritage Trail says it is still sold in Burlington County.
music: I Got a Stick Arr Bryan Teoh by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: From Goat Town to the World's Largest Watch Case Maker
stories.blurb: The Delaware River Heritage Trail says that in 1850 the area was a settlement of squatter farms known as Goat Town. <short pause> The Riverside Historical Society says Samuel Bechtold founded the town the next year as a resort called Progress. <short pause> The Heritage Trail says it was renamed Riverside in 1867. <short pause> It says a watchcase maker, Theophilus Zurbrugg, moved his factory there in 1892. <short pause> The society says Riverside once housed the world's largest watchcase manufacturer.
music: Cold Funk by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Quiet Village That Became Camp Dix
stories.blurb: The Burlington County Times says that on June 1st, 1917, a captain and 19 soldiers arrived in Wrightstown to begin an army training camp. <short pause> A photographic exhibit says that before that June, few people outside New Jersey had heard of the village. <short pause> The newspaper says Camp Dix was formally established on July 18th and named for Major General John Adams Dix. <short pause> By the end of the war, it says the camp had over 1,600 buildings, the largest military installation in the Northeast.
music: Port Horizon by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Elvis at Fort Dix
stories.blurb: Camp Dix became a permanent army post and was renamed Fort Dix in 1939. <short pause> The Burlington County Times lists the singer Elvis Presley's discharge from the army at Fort Dix in March of 1960. <short pause> A photo caption in the National Archive collection shows Sergeant Presley receiving a gift from Nancy Sinatra at a press conference there.
stories.flag: Sources differ on the exact discharge date (March 3 in the newspaper timeline, March 5 on the archive photo record), so only the month is stated.
music: Vibe Ace by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Once Called White Hill
stories.blurb: Fieldsboro was once known as White Hill. <short pause> The borough says the state legislature incorporated it in March of 1850. <short pause> The borough history says a Scottish gardener, George McLean, who had been head gardener at Joseph Bonaparte's Point Breeze estate in Bordentown, later moved to Fieldsboro.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the gardener detail: the borough website. The former name White Hill is also in NJ Archive.
music: Rite of Passage by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: How Chester Township Became Maple Shade
stories.blurb: In 1688, a large area of Burlington County was called Chester Township. <short pause> The township says that area included what are now Maple Shade, Moorestown, Cinnaminson, Palmyra, Riverton, Delran, and Riverside. <short pause> A local history site says Moorestown separated in 1922, leaving Maple Shade as the last part of Chester Township. <short pause> It says on November 6, 1945, voters approved the name Maple Shade by 1,067 to 74.
music: Chill by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Brotherton Reservation
stories.blurb: In 1758, the colony bought land in Shamong for native people living south of the Raritan River. <short pause> A 1955 place names book says it was called Brotherton and that most of the Indians moved there in 1759. <short pause> The Pinelands Commission says it was one of the first reservations in North America. <short pause> The place names book says the reservation lasted until 1801 when the Brotherton Indians asked to move to Oneida Lake in New York.
music: Dreamer by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Capital of the Pine Barrens
stories.blurb: The village of Chatsworth in Woodland Township is called the Capital of the Pine Barrens. <short pause> The Cranberry Festival's history page says the township covers over 96 square miles and has about 2,000 residents, the largest township with the smallest population in the county. <short pause> It says cranberries came into the picture in the late 1800s. <short pause> The National Register nomination for Buzby's General Store says the white cedar building went up about 1865.
music: Arid Foothills by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Tavern on the Footpath
stories.blurb: Burlington Township says that in 1666, three Dutchmen settled along the Delaware River and built a log cabin. <short pause> It says the cabin served as the only tavern in that part of the country. <short pause> The township says it stood by a narrow footpath used by travelers going from Manhattan toward Virginia. <short pause> It says the township was established in 1677.
stories.flag: SINGLE source: the township website.
music: Daily Beetle by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The First Company Town in Burlington County
stories.blurb: Pemberton Borough's history says David Budd had a mill on Budd's Run as early as 1740. <short pause> In 1752, it says he and three others formed the New Mills Company, which built saw and grist mills on the Rancocas and planned a company town. <short pause> The National Register nomination calls it the first company town in Burlington County. <short pause> The borough says that by 1785, the company also ran a tanyard, two forges, and a fulling mill.
music: Neo Western by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The First Quaker Meeting in the County
stories.blurb: The Delaware River Heritage Trail says English Quakers first arrived in Mansfield Township in 1677. <short pause> It says William Biddle, a Quaker born in London who had been imprisoned for his beliefs, settled there in 1681. <short pause> The trail says the house he built around 1684 was the site of the first Quaker meeting in Burlington County. <short pause> It says the township was created in 1688 and reportedly named for a market town in Nottinghamshire.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the Biddle house detail: the Delaware River Heritage Trail.
music: What Is Love by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Navy's First Submarine Was Tested Here
stories.blurb: The Delanco Township history says the inventor Brutus de Villeroi tested his Alligator submarine on the Rancocas Creek. <short pause> The township timeline says the prototype was 33 feet long and was tested for three months. <short pause> It says he claimed it was built mainly for undersea salvage, not for military use. <short pause> The township says its successor became the U.S. Navy's first commissioned submarine. <short pause> A township article says the inventor and his crew stayed in a hotel in Delanco.
stories.flag: No year given: the township's own pages differ (1859 vs 1861).
music: Ossuary 5 - Rest by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Camp Meeting Grounds
stories.blurb: The camp's own history says it was founded in 1898 as a camp meeting association. <short pause> It says a group of Methodist ministers founded it in the township. <short pause> It says that around 1963 a car crashed into one of the camp's buildings. <short pause> It says the crash convinced the board to move the camp to a larger property. <short pause> It says the camp officially moved to a new site in Tabernacle in June of 1965.
stories.flag: Single source: Delanco Camp history page (Fletcher Grove Camp Meeting Association, Delanco; moved to Lake Agape).
music: Laid Back Guitars by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Resort Built Entirely of Logs
stories.blurb: Medford Lakes started as a resort with a unique idea. <short pause> The borough says every building would be made of logs. <short pause> It says shiploads of cedar logs were imported and craftsmen shaped them into homes. <short pause> The borough says log cabins were built exclusively through the 1930s and into the 40s, and that by the 50s, the full log rule was relaxed to allow simulated log siding. <short pause> It became an independent borough in 1939.
music: Ossuary 1 - A Beginning by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Colony Club, the Camp and the Golf Course
stories.blurb: The Medford Lakes Development Company was formed in 1927. <short pause> The borough says the Colony Club Pavilion was built the next year on ground the company donated. <short pause> Construction of the golf course began in 1929. <short pause> The borough says the camp began in 1930 and the Log Cabin Hotel was built in 1931. <short pause> It says the pavilion collapsed in a snow storm in 1938 and the Vaughn Community House was built afterward.
stories.flag: SINGLE source: the borough website. Golf entry is history only, no fees.
music: Still Pickin by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: New Jersey's First State Forest
stories.blurb: The state Department of Environmental Protection says Bass River State Forest, established in 1905, is New Jersey's first state forest. <short pause> It says a Civilian Conservation Corps camp worked there from 1933 to 1942. <short pause> A Pine Barrens history site says about 200 men ordinarily lived at the camp. <short pause> The state says they planted 4,500 acres of timber and built bridges. <short pause> They also created Lake Absegami, by damming two streams.
music: Stay the Course by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: A Township Mostly Owned by the Military
stories.blurb: New Hanover Township says it covers about 22 square miles. <short pause> It says 90% of the township is owned by the federal government and occupied by McGuire Air Force Base and Fort Dix. <short pause> The township says Cookstown, its seat, was named for William Cooke, who operated a grist mill built in 1721. <short pause> It says Cooke bought the mill in 1776.
stories.flag: SINGLE source: the township website. A boundary date on its page was left out because it cannot be reconciled.
music: Joey's Formal Waltz - Unscented by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Long Bridge
stories.blurb: Hainesport was once known as Long Bridge. <short pause> The county parks department says the name came from a long wooden toll bridge over the Rancocas Creek, on the road from Mount Holly to Moorestown. <short pause> It says that in 1778, American patriots partly dismantled the bridge to delay the British march. <short pause> The county says that in 1847, Barclay Haines bought 50 acres there and started a small settlement. <short pause> It says by early 1852, the community was known as Hainesport.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the 1778 bridge detail: the county parks history.
music: Universal by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Port Far From the Sea
stories.blurb: The Philadelphia Inquirer says it is hard to imagine why a place so far from the ocean has port in its name. <short pause> It says the township was originally called Long Bridge and was renamed in 1850 when Barclay Haines built a wharf on the south branch of a nearby creek. <short pause> The township says sidewheeler steamboats carried freight and passengers between the wharf and Philadelphia. <short pause> It says freight wagons and stagecoaches met there, making the town the headquarters for steamer navigation on the creek. <short pause> It says the arrival of the railroad brought about the end of the steamship era.
music: Chillin Hard by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Parker Mill
stories.blurb: Eastampton Township says that around 1683, Delaware Indians lived in the area. <short pause> The township says a mill called Parker Mills was running on the Rancocas Creek by 1790. <short pause> It says two neighbors fought lawsuits over mills for 12 years, ending in 1802. <short pause> The state archive says the township was created from part of Westampton by an act passed on February 11, 1880.
music: Jellyfish in Space by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The First Nearly Complete Dinosaur (Hadrosaurus foulkii)
stories.blurb: The state legislature found that the dinosaur Hadrosaurus was the first nearly complete dinosaur skeleton discovered virtually intact anywhere in the world. <short pause> It says it was unearthed in October of 1858 in a marl pit in Haddonfield. <short pause> The state library says a farmer first found large bones in his field in the late 1830s. <short pause> It says the anatomist Joseph Leidy and a lawyer and amateur geologist named William Parker Foulke excavated the land and found the skeleton with only the skull missing. <short pause> The Haddonfield borough says it became the first mounted dinosaur skeleton displayed anywhere in the world in 1868.
music: Heart of Nowhere by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Fourth Graders Who Passed a Law
stories.blurb: The state library says that in 1988, a fourth-grade teacher at Strawbridge Elementary School in Haddon Township guided her class in proposing Hadrosaurus as New Jersey's official state dinosaur. <short pause> It says the effort took four years and hundreds of letters. <short pause> It says 97 students took part. <short pause> On June 13, 1991, almost 100 children toured the State House and watched the governor sign the bill.
music: Teddy Bear Waltz by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: How Delaware Township Became Cherry Hill
stories.blurb: The township says that on March 13th, 1844, residents held a town meeting and incorporated it as Delaware Township. <short pause> WHYY says it had no post office of its own, so mail went through neighboring towns. <short pause> It says a Delaware Township post office already existed in Hunterdon County, so the Post Office Department insisted on a new name. <short pause> WHYY says a different name was nearly approved until a developer and his publicity director lobbied for Cherry Hill to publicize his Cherry Hill Inn. <short pause> The township changed its name in 1961.
music: Deuces by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Racetrack That Built Cherry Hill
stories.blurb: A Camden history site says Garden State Park opened in 1942 after delays from wartime rationing. <short pause> It says war authorities seized 30,000 tons of structural steel, so the grandstand was mostly built of wood. <short pause> The Courier-Post says the seeds of Cherry Hill were planted on July 18, 1942, the day the track opened. <short pause> The history site says its success sparked entertainment growth in what was then rural Delaware Township. <short pause> It says that included the Cherry Hill Shopping Center in 1961, today's Cherry Hill Mall, the first enclosed shopping mall on the East Coast.
music: Leblon by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Last Card at Garden State Park
stories.blurb: The Associated Press said Garden State Park staged its final card on Thursday, May 3rd, 2001. <short pause> It called it a 58-year-old track that had hosted the likes of Citation and Secretariat. <short pause> It said the track will be razed for shops, offices, and homes on the 225-acre site. <short pause> A Camden history site says a fire broke out in the track's restaurant kitchen on April 14th, 1977, during a racing program. <short pause> It says the wooden grandstand lasted long enough for more than 11,000 patrons and employees to escape.
stories.flag: A fire story. No injuries or names are described; only the escape of more than 11,000 people is stated.
music: Longing and Concern by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Where Campbell's Soup Began
stories.blurb: Campbell says it was founded in 1869 by a fruit merchant named Joseph Campbell and a commercial canner named Abraham Anderson. <short pause> The company's archives say it began in Camden, New Jersey. <short pause> The city of Camden also says Campbell Soup Company was born there. <short pause> Campbell says the firm was first called Anderson and Campbell and later claimed the name Campbell Soup Company.
music: Valse Gymnopedie by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Paper Souper Dress
stories.blurb: A Campbell's archivist says Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans were first exhibited in 1962. <short pause> In 1967, the company released the Souper Dress, a paper dress with the repeating red and white label pattern. <short pause> To get one, you sent labels from two kinds of Campbell's vegetable soups plus $1. <short pause> The archivist says the dress was a hit, but because it was disposable, few have survived. <short pause> The company archive holds four.
stories.flag: SINGLE source: a Campbell's archivist blog post.
music: Verano Sensual by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Dutch Fort on the Delaware
stories.blurb: Gloucester City says that in 1623, Captain Cornelius Mey and 24 Dutch settlers landed at Gloucester Point and built Fort Nassau. <short pause> It was a fort and trading post for furs. <short pause> The city says it could command the river and existed for 25 years. <short pause> The city says it was the first Dutch fortified settlement on the Delaware.
music: Heroic Age by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Oldest Meeting on a Street Corner
stories.blurb: A park page says the West Jersey Proprietors have met in the city at noon on April 13th since 1688. <short pause> It says they meet to elect the proprietors who attend the general meeting in Burlington in May. <short pause> It says the proprietors were responsible for selling and recording the sale of available land in Western New Jersey. <short pause> The New York Times reported in April of 2001 that one of the country's oldest existing corporations convened on a street corner there. <short pause> It said five minutes later, business was concluded and its members went off to lunch.
music: Vivacity by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Born After the Blizzard of '88
stories.blurb: Collingswood's history says that two months after the blizzard of 1888, residents of the western section of Haddon Township decided to strike out on their own. <short pause> Collingswood elected its first borough council in 1888. <short pause> The history says the settlers' early name for the area was Newton. <short pause> A local historic house site says the borough was laid out around a 100-acre triangle of parkland.
music: Zazie by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Saturday Farmers' Market
stories.blurb: The town's farmers market says it began in the year 2000 as a project of a civic group called Proud Neighbors. <short pause> It says it is now a project of the borough. <short pause> It says it is held every Saturday from May through Thanksgiving. <short pause> It says it sits under the PATCO high-speed line near two massive blue water towers. <short pause> It says New Jersey Monthly honored it as best farm stand with the comment authentic rural feel and hustle bustle.
stories.flag: Single source: Collingswood Farmers' Market's own history page.
music: Lively Lumpsucker by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Skiing in South Jersey
stories.blurb: DCSki says Ski Mountain in Pine Hill opened in January of 1965, about 10 miles from the Philadelphia area. <short pause> It says it had snowmaking and a three-story lodge. <short pause> A double chairlift, 1,800 feet long, was added in 1978. <short pause> A radio station says that in some summers it became Action Mountain with waterslides. <short pause> DCSki says the operation filed for bankruptcy in 1986. <short pause> The radio station says a golf course was built on the old ski mountain in the late 1990s.
stories.flag: Golf mention is history only, no fees.
music: Mischief Maker by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Highest Point in Camden County
stories.blurb: The Pine Hill borough history says the town was named for its pine trees and hills. <short pause> It says people came here for their health because the climate was considered healthy. <short pause> The borough says the New Jersey Almanac lists it as the highest point in Camden County at 214 feet. <short pause> It became a borough in 1929. <short pause> One of the council's first ordinances required residents to clear tree stumps from the streets by August 1st, 1930 or be fined $5.
stories.flag: SINGLE source: the borough website.
music: Jazz Brunch by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Name from a German Book
stories.blurb: Lindenwold became a borough on April 23rd, 1929. <short pause> The borough says its first official meeting was held in the old fire hall at Linden Avenue and Berlin Road. <short pause> It says the name, German for linden woods, was suggested by a local resident who had been reading a German book. <short pause> The borough says he wanted linden trees planted along the streets, but officials chose cheaper trees instead.
music: Broken Reality by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The End of the Line
stories.blurb: The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia says a new high-speed rail line opened in 1969 and was an immediate success. <short pause> It says the route from Camden to the end of the line was built on the right-of-way of the railroad to Atlantic City. <short pause> It says the trains were among the first to be operated by computer. <short pause> It says the line used an innovative advanced fare collection system. <short pause> It says it initially carried 21,000 riders daily.
stories.flag: Single source: PATCO Speedline computer operation, fare system and ridership details are from the Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia only.
music: Cuban Sandwich by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Named for a Governor
stories.blurb: Voorhees Township says it was named in honor of Foster McGowan Voorhees, the governor of New Jersey. <short pause> It says he granted the petition for Voorhees to become a separate township on March 3, 1899. <short pause> It had been part of Waterford Township. <short pause> The township says Voor is a Dutch prefix meaning in front of. <short pause> It says Hees was a village near Ruinen in Drenthe, Holland.
music: Mystery Bazaar by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Three Villages Vote to Become One
stories.blurb: Audubon's police history says developers had started building on the land before the turn of the century. <short pause> It says the first area was called Orston after a town in Nottingham, England. <short pause> The second development was Audubon. <short pause> It says residents of the separate communities voted in 1904 at the Logan Memorial Presbyterian Church to become one town. <short pause> Audubon was incorporated in 1905 with about 800 people. <short pause> Until then, the communities were part of Haddon Township.
stories.flag: SINGLE source for the church vote detail: the borough police history page.
music: Enchanted Valley by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Naturalist Next Door
stories.blurb: The blog Hidden New Jersey says the famous naturalist John James Audubon lived in Camden between 1829 and 1832. <short pause> It says he found his own birding spot along a stream in what was then Haddon Township. <short pause> Wikipedia says that on March 13, 1905, the borough was created from parts of Haddon Township and named for him. <short pause> The blog quotes his diary on Great Egg Harbor. <short pause> It says the naturalist wrote that except for the Florida Keys, it probably affords as varied a field as any part of the Atlantic seaboard.
music: Dreamy Flashback by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: America's First Traffic Circle
stories.blurb: A local history column says the airport circle in Pennsauken opened in 1925, the first traffic circle in the United States. <short pause> The Star-Ledger calls it the first rotary of its kind in the country. <short pause> The column says it was associated with Central Airport, which opened in 1929. <short pause> It says the airport gradually gave up commercial flights after Philadelphia International opened in 1939. <short pause> It says the property was sold in 1952 for $1 million to build a shopping area, and the airport closed in 1957.

stories.title: The First Drive-In Movie
stories.blurb: Guinness World Records says Richard Hollingshead was issued the first drive-in theater patent on May 16, 1933. <short pause> It says he opened the first one on June 6, 1933, on a site for 400 cars. <short pause> A state history lesson says moviegoers in Pennsauken made history that night. <short pause> Camden County says it opened on Crescent Boulevard in Camden. <short pause> The county says people paid 25 cents each and 25 cents per car, with no group charged more than a dollar.

stories.title: The Airport Before Philadelphia's
stories.blurb: Wikipedia says Camden Central Airport in the township was the main airport for Philadelphia in the 1930s. <short pause> It says it started operations in 1929. <short pause> A Camden history site says it was the prime air connection between the Philadelphia area and the world for about 12 years. <short pause> It says airmail was carried by autogiro to the roof of a post office in Philadelphia. <short pause> It says that when Philadelphia's own airport opened in June of 1940, the four airlines left the field. <short pause> It says the field then trained naval and marine aviators in yellow biplanes.
stories.flag: The airport was in Pennsauken Township. The two sources differ on August versus September 1929 for the start, so only the year is given.

stories.title: The Glassworks and the Blue Anchor Inn
stories.blurb: The Winslow Township Historical Society says the township was created on March 8, 1845, from part of Gloucester Township. <short pause> It says the first town meeting was held at the Blue Anchor Inn. <short pause> The society says the township covers about 58 square miles, made up of many small villages. <short pause> It says a glass factory owned by William Coffin and Andrew Hay was documented in 1833. <short pause> By 1865, it says the factory employed 400 people. <short pause> It says the factory was destroyed by fire in 1892.

stories.title: A Town Born from Railroad Rumors
stories.blurb: Merchantville's borough history says the area was primarily farmland until about 1851. <short pause> It says rumors of the coming railroad were the impetus for land acquisition. <short pause> The town was originally part of Stockton Township. <short pause> The borough says its citizens petitioned the state to become an incorporated borough, effective May 18, 1874. <short pause> It says a second period of growth came in the automobile age, when feasibility studies for the Benjamin Franklin Bridge began in 1914.

stories.title: A Free Community Before the Civil War
stories.blurb: The borough's website says that in 1840, land was purchased by abolitionists for freed and escaped slaves. <short pause> It says the governor signed a law on March 23rd, 1926, incorporating the borough. <short pause> The borough says its first election on April 20th made it the first independent, self-governing African American community north of the Mason-Dixon line. <short pause> It says a farmer named Peter Mott gave refuge to escaping slaves and took part in the Underground Railroad.

stories.title: Mount Pisgah and Snow Hill
stories.blurb: The church's own history says its story began in 1792 with meetings in farm homes. <short pause> The Peter Mott House site says it was first named Snow Hill Church and started as a multi-racial congregation. <short pause> Both say the first church building was built in 1808. <short pause> The church says a circuit rider, Reverend Richard Allen, preached at Free Haven, which is now the borough. <short pause> It says a vote kept the property with those who supported him, and the church later became part of the African Methodist Episcopal Church. <short pause> The church says the current building was built in 1911 and that many local churches were born out of it.

stories.title: The Borough That Exists for Sunday Golf
stories.blurb: Tavistock's Borough website says it was incorporated on February 16, 1921. <short pause> It says the founding is said to have been driven by the fact that Haddonfield was a dry borough. <short pause> The borough says it was formed to allow members of the Tavistock Country Club to play golf on Sunday. <short pause> It says the borough covers just 0.28 square miles.

stories.title: The Paint Works on Silver Lake
stories.blurb: A Sherwin-Williams site says the Gibbsboro property was first a sawmill and later a grain mill. <short pause> It says the Lucas company converted it into a paint and varnish factory. <short pause> A local history says the company developed ready-mixed paint, known for its shades of green. <short pause> It says the paint works employed 300 men in 1886 and 700 in 1909. <short pause> Sherwin-Williams says it bought the Lucas company in 1930 and the plant closed in 1978.

stories.title: The Paint Works and the Superfund List
stories.blurb: The Environmental Protection Agency says that on March 19th, 2008, it added a former paint factory site in the borough to the federal Superfund list. <short pause> It says the site was a paint manufacturing facility run from the mid-1800s by John Lucas and Company and eventually by Sherwin-Williams. <short pause> It says Sherwin-Williams acquired the property in 1930. <short pause> The agency says decades of waste discharge into a nearby creek and leaking tanks and drums led to widespread contamination. <short pause> It says the soil and groundwater under the former plant were contaminated, as well as some sediment in and near the creek.

stories.title: The Oldest Railroad Station in New Jersey
stories.blurb: The National Register nomination for the Long-a-Coming Depot in Berlin says it was built in 1856. <short pause> It calls it the oldest railroad station known to survive in New Jersey. <short pause> The Long-a-Coming Historical Society says a rail line was laid in 1853 and the station was built three years later. <short pause> It says the town sat halfway between Philadelphia and Atlantic City.

stories.title: Long-a-Coming
stories.blurb: The Long A Coming Historical Society says there are many stories of how the town got its name. <short pause> It says a favorite version starts with a Native American path that ran through the area. <short pause> It says travelers stopped at a stream here and called the spot Long A Coming. <short pause> Wikipedia says another tradition cites early European visitors who found a stream at the head of the Great Egg Harbor River. <short pause> It says the place was known in earlier times as Long A Coming. <short pause> A historic district listing says the village was renamed Berlin in 1872.

stories.title: The Trolley Park That Lasted a Century
stories.blurb: PhillyVoice says Clementon Park opened in 1907 as a trolley park. <short pause> It says it was meant to boost weekend ridership on a transit line from South Jersey to Philadelphia. <short pause> The water park was added in 2003. <short pause> The Inquirer says the park closed abruptly in 2019 before being purchased at a public auction.

stories.title: The Jack Rabbit Coaster
stories.blurb: The Philadelphia Inquirer says the amusement park opened in 1907. <short pause> It says the most notable long-standing attraction was the Jack Rabbit, a wooden coaster. <short pause> It says the ride was considered state-of-the-art when it opened in 1919. <short pause> The Inquirer says that after 83 years, it was one of the oldest operating roller coasters in the world when it closed in 2002. <short pause> A coaster enthusiast site says it sat unused from 2003 to 2007 and was demolished in December of 2007.

stories.title: New Jersey's First Official Drag Strip

stories.title: The Hessians at the Mill Dam

Bell, who owned and operated Bell Farm. <short pause> The Courier-Post says it honors the Bell family, prominent horse breeders and landowners.

stories.title: The Ritz Theatre

stories.title: Named for a Quaker Pioneer's Father

stories.title: Named for the Heights

stories.title: The Station That Stayed

stories.title: The Amusement Park That Became a Borough

stories.title: The Little Town With National Titles

https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Watch the Tram Car
stories.blurb: A Wildwood's fact sheet says the five original electric tram car trains were custom built for the 1939 New York World's Fair. <short pause> It says they were called Greyhound trackless trains. <short pause> It says a Wildwood businessman bought them and put them in service on the boardwalk on June 11th, 1949. <short pause> A tram car website says the one-way fare was 10 cents. <short pause> It says the tram cars carry hundreds of thousands of guests each year.
music: Allada by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Four Ministers and a Cedar Tree
stories.blurb: The Ocean City Historical Museum says that in 1879, four Methodist ministers came to the island to establish a resort based on Christian values. <short pause> A city walking tour brochure says a cedar tree shaded them as they met. <short pause> It says the trunk of that tree now has a home at the museum. <short pause> Visit NJ Shore says the island was first called Peck's Beach, and the ministers renamed it Ocean City. <short pause> It says the first lots were sold in May of 1880, and by October, there were 51 buildings.
music: Drone in D by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: No Swimming on Sunday
stories.blurb: Visit NJ Shore says the town is well known for prohibiting the sale of alcoholic beverages within its limits. <short pause> It says that on July 5th, 1881, the Ocean City Association adopted laws forbidding swimming, riding, or driving on Sunday. <short pause> It says the city council passed more laws in 1885 to restrict bathing on Sundays. <short pause> It says the town also hosted a temperance convention in August of 1885.
stories.flag: Single source: Visit NJ Shore history page.
music: Poppers and Prosecco by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Music Pier
stories.blurb: The city of Ocean City says construction of the Music Pier began in 1928 after the community lost a large part of its boardwalk to a fire in 1927. <short pause> It says the pier was dedicated on July 4th, 1929. <short pause> It says the municipal orchestra entertained crowds twice a day, seven days a week. <short pause> Atlantic City Weekly also says the Music Pier opened in 1929.
music: Thinking of You by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Queen of the Seaside Resorts
stories.blurb: The city of Cape May says that from 1766, Cape Island developed as a place where many came for their health and pleasure. <short pause> It says a two-week stay by Henry Clay in 1847 reinforced its position as the major seaside retreat in the country. <short pause> It says investors began building the largest hotel in the world, the Mount Vernon Hotel, in 1852 to serve 3,500 patrons. <short pause> It says the unfinished hotel burned in 1856 while it held 2,100 guests.
stories.flag: Single source: City of Cape May pages.
music: Wisps of Whorls by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Fire That Saved Victorian Cape May
stories.blurb: The city of Cape May says the most devastating fire of all, in 1878, destroyed 35 acres of the city, from Congress Hall over to Ocean Street. <short pause> It says the city rebuilt itself on a smaller scale, in Queen Anne, Gothic, and American bracketed styles. <short pause> It says the decision not to compete with modern, popular resorts preserved the town's character. <short pause> The city says Cape May is a National Historic Landmark, with the second largest collection of Victorian houses behind San Francisco.
stories.flag: Single source: City of Cape May pages.
music: Wet Riffs by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Tommy's Folly
stories.blurb: Wikipedia says Congress Hall was first built in 1816 as a wooden boarding house, and its proprietor called it the Big House. <short pause> It says locals, thinking it too big to succeed, called it Tommy's Folly. <short pause> It says the hotel burned to the ground in the Great Fire of 1878 and within a year was rebuilt in brick to convince leery guests it was fireproof. <short pause> It says presidents Pierce, Buchanan, Grant, and Harrison vacationed there, and Harrison made it his summer White House. <short pause> The city of Cape May also lists visits from presidents Pierce and Harrison.
music: Organic Meditations Two by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Stick-Style Mansion
stories.blurb: A New Jersey state site says the estate was constructed in 1879 and is an outstanding example of Victorian stick-style architecture. <short pause> It attributes the building to a prominent Philadelphia architect. <short pause> It says its character includes ornate inverted chimneys, an arcaded porch, and dormers. <short pause> Wikipedia says the mansion has 18 rooms. <short pause> The Mid-Atlantic Center for the Arts calls it Cape May's only Victorian house museum.
music: Eastminster by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Ferry to Delaware
stories.blurb: The Delaware Public Archives says the ferry across the bay to Delaware was dedicated on June 30th, 1964. <short pause> It says the fleet carries passengers and automobiles on an 80-minute crossing. <short pause> The Cape Gazette says the idea of a crossing dates back to the 19th century. <short pause> It says several failed attempts, including an entrepreneur who planned to use experimental concrete ships, eventually led to the formation of the Delaware River and Bay Authority in 1962.
music: Lagoa v2 by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: A City Like Venice
stories.blurb: Wikipedia says the developer Charles Landis, who also founded Vineland, bought the island in 1880. <short pause> It says he intended to build a city like Venice, Italy. <short pause> Wikipedia says Sea Isle City was first incorporated as a borough on May 22, 1882, from portions of Dennis Township after a referendum held six days earlier. <short pause> It says the borough was reincorporated on March 31, 1890.
stories.flag: Single source: Wikipedia.
music: Kawai Kitsune by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Bird Sanctuary
stories.blurb: Wikipedia says herons began nesting in the area that became the bird sanctuary around 1938. <short pause> It says the town protected the site by local ordinance in 1947 and put up a fence around it in 1961. <short pause> It says that as of 1964, more than 5,000 birds would arrive for nesting season. <short pause> It says the sanctuary was designated a National Natural Landmark in October 1965, the first in New Jersey.
stories.flag: Single source: Wikipedia.
music: Wood and Metal and Water by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: A Haven for Persecuted Families
stories.blurb: The borough website says the town was founded in 1891 as a haven for Eastern European Jews who were persecuted in the tsarist pogroms. <short pause> It says a fund purchased 5,300 acres in Dennis Township to start a settlement. <short pause> It says that within two years the settlers cleared the forest and built a town and farms. <short pause> JewishGen says it was incorporated in 1903. <short pause> The borough website says it became known as the first self-governed Jewish community since the fall of Jerusalem.
music: Cool Vibes by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Brotherhood Synagogue
stories.blurb: JewishGen says the Woodbine Brotherhood built the Brotherhood Synagogue, which was dedicated in 1896. <short pause> The National Register nomination says it was the religious, cultural, and educational center of a colony of East European Jewish immigrants. <short pause> It says it was constructed entirely by the colonists on an American design. <short pause> JewishGen says it is now a national historic landmark and houses a museum of Woodbine heritage.
music: Bumba Crossing by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: An Island Named for King Arthur's Resting Place
stories.blurb: Visit NJ Shore says one man bought the island in December 1722 reportedly for £79. <short pause> It says his family owned what was then called Seven Mile Beach for the next 100 years. <short pause> It says the Seven Mile Beach Company bought it in 1887 and founded Avalon in the north and Stone Harbor in the south. <short pause> A news site says the Reverend Charles Bond, a devoted fan of King Arthur, named Avalon after the legendary place where Arthur was said to be buried.
music: Avec Soin by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Lighthouse That Moved
stories.blurb: The Coast Guard's history page says the lighthouse was completed on April 16, 1874. <short pause> It says the government bought the 1.5-acre site for $150. <short pause> It says that in August of 1913, a severe storm damaged the foundation and the lighthouse was moved 150 feet westward. <short pause> It says a fire in May of 1938 caused extensive damage. <short pause> It says the lighthouse was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977 after restoration by the city.
music: Facile by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Where Doo Wop Got Its Name
stories.blurb: The town's historical society says doo-wop is a term coined by the Mid-Atlantic Center for the Arts in the early 1990s. <short pause> It says it describes the space-age style of the 1950s and '60s with sweeping angles, bright colors, starbursts, boomerang shapes, and plastic palm trees. <short pause> It says the first motel in this style in the town was the Ebb Tide Motel, built in 1957. <short pause> Smithsonian magazine says nearly 300 motels were built along this five-mile stretch of the shore in the 1950s and '60s.
music: Kings of Tara by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Three Lighthouses
stories.blurb: The Coast Guard's history page says the first Cape May lighthouse was built in 1823, west of the present tower at a site that is now underwater. <short pause> It says it was lost to erosion. <short pause> It says a second tower built in 1847 was demolished around 1859 because of poor construction. <short pause> It says the existing tower, 157 feet tall, was first lit in 1859. <short pause> The city of Cape May also says a new lighthouse was built in 1859 and still exists today.
music: Organic Meditations Three by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Concrete Ship at Sunset Beach
stories.blurb: The Sunset Beach website says that because of a critical steel shortage during World War I, the federal government turned to experimental concrete ships. <short pause> Wikipedia says this ship was the first of 12 concrete ships for the Emergency Fleet to finish construction. <short pause> A concrete ship site says she was launched in Georgia on December 5th, 1918, a month after the war ended. <short pause> It says she was used to carry troops home from Europe and coal in New England. <short pause> Atlas Obscura says she ran aground on June 8th, 1926, and her wreck lies 150 ft off Sunset Beach.
music: Achilles by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Cape May Diamonds
stories.blurb: Wikipedia says Cape May diamonds are quartz pebbles found on the beaches of Cape May Point. <short pause> It says they are sometimes cut and polished to resemble diamonds and sold as souvenirs. <short pause> It says they are most abundant at Sunset Beach and one neighboring beach. <short pause> The Sunset Beach website says that, according to local legend, the area's first people who discovered them believed the crystals held supernatural powers. <short pause> New Jersey Monthly says they are not diamonds at all, but begin in the upper reaches of the Delaware River.
music: Eastern Thought by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Farmsteads, a Legend, and a Colonial House
stories.blurb: The borough says West Cape May was incorporated in 1884. <short pause> A historical marker says that as early as the 1690s, farmsteads dotted the area. <short pause> It says legend has it that when the Lenape crossed the Delaware Bay in 1695, they met a farmer plowing his fields. <short pause> The borough says a timber frame home built about 1715 is one of the oldest houses on Cape Island. <short pause> It says the historic core was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976.
music: Infinite Perspective by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Five Mile Island's Tiny Borough
stories.blurb: A news site says West Wildwood was incorporated as a borough in 1920 from portions of Middle Township. <short pause> It says the borough sits on an island nicknamed Five Mile Island, connected to the mainland by a single bridge. <short pause> It ranks it among the 30 smallest municipalities in New Jersey, with a population of 566. <short pause> A 2008 New York Times piece says the island had no schools, but one bar, one liquor store, one mini golf course, and one church.
music: Voice Over Under by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Township That Gave Birth to Ocean City
stories.blurb: Wikipedia says Upper Township was formed as a precinct on April 2nd, 1723. <short pause> It says it was incorporated by an act of the state legislature on February 21st, 1798. <short pause> It says portions of it were taken to form Dennis Township on March 1st, 1827, and Ocean City on March 3rd, 1884. <short pause> The township's own history page says it was one of the original townships created under the Township Act.
music: Space 1990-B by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Birth Place of South Jersey
stories.blurb: The Cape May County website says Lower Township was first settled by whalers from New England and Long Island around 1635. <short pause> It says the area is often called the birthplace of South Jersey. <short pause> The township says that sometime around 1640, whalers following the whales set up temporary settlements at what is now Town Bank. <short pause> It says the settlements were abandoned each year as the whalers followed the whales. <short pause> It says the county was divided in 1723 into three precincts, Upper, Middle, and Lower.
music: Sunday Dub by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Where the County Held Its First Meeting
stories.blurb: The Cape May County history page says the first town meeting was held on February 7th, 1692 at the home of Benjamin Godfrey. <short pause> It says the county's first sheriff officially took office at that meeting. <short pause> It says the sheriff has overseen the county jail since 1705. <short pause> The county says Middle Township serves as the county seat with a historic district on Main Street of buildings more than a century old.
music: Light Thought var 2 by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: Ships on Dennis Creek
stories.blurb: A historical background document says Dennisville was originally a fishing village where ships were built on Dennis Creek and launched on the Delaware Bay. <short pause> It says that in 1687, John Dennis and several whalers from New England and Long Island bought land from the local native people and established the first permanent community. <short pause> The township museum says the name Dennisville was adopted in 1854. <short pause> Wikipedia says Dennis Township was formed from Upper Township on March 1st, 1827.
music: Organic Meditations One by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

stories.title: The Shingle Miners
stories.blurb: The Cape May County Historical Society says that in the 1800s, one of the county's local products was white cedar lumber. <short pause> It says an unusual offshoot, shingle mining, prospered until the late 1800s. <short pause> It describes shingle mining as raising white cedar logs from the muck of the cedar swamps nearby. <short pause> It says the logs had been buried for centuries. <short pause> The township museum says the supply of ancient submerged trees was depleted at the end of the 19th century. <short pause> It says the shingles for the roof of Independence Hall were supplied by a local shingle miner's father and a partner who won a contract for 25,000 shingles.
stories.flag: Single source: Independence Hall shingle detail is from the Dennis Township Museum page only.
music: Meditation Impromptu 01 by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0
